page: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a dedicated 96-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features a single thread per physical core, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include integrated local storage or GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional multi-core efficiency and memory subsystem performance. The D96pls_v6 achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core execution, including software compilation tasks. Its memory bandwidth is highly competitive, scoring in the top decile for both cached and uncached read/write operations. However, single-core performance remains average, as demonstrated by single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench scores.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D96pls_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the absence of bundled local storage. Additionally, as an ARM64 platform, it lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX or AMX. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high compute density and excellent multi-threaded throughput per resource unit, making it a cost-effective choice for highly parallelizable workloads that do not demand large memory footprints.

This server is highly suited for multi-threaded, compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and Redis deployments. It is also capable of handling medium-to-large LLM inference text generation tasks, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or workloads requiring local high-speed scratch disks.
